name: Church's

origin: Founded in 1873 in Northampton, England by Thomas Church with wife Eliza and sons Alfred and William (family shoemaking traced to Anthony Church, 1617).

cities: No store of its own in the US · department stores, and its own site

craft_evidence.owned: yes: Church & Co ltd, Northampton, listed as Manufacturing in Prada Group structure (AR 2025 p.43); brand history names St James Road HQ/factory since 1957; Prada lists 1 owned UK industrial facility
craft_evidence.makers: no: PDPs state town/country only (Made in Northampton, England / Made in Italy); Italian maker never named
craft_evidence.mills: no: no tannery or leather supplier named on PDPs sampled
craft_evidence.madein: 11 of 12 sampled men's PDPs across 6 categories state origin (6 England/Northampton, 5 Italy: sneakers, sandal, a Chelsea boot, a slipper); 1 sandal PDP states none
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: family shoemaking from 1617; first factory 1873 at 30 Maple Street, Northampton; Duke Street 1880; St James Road 1957; Prada 1999
craft_evidence.process: partial: PDPs state Goodyear welted construction, last numbers, hand-stitched aprons, hand-driven nails (Royal Collection); Prada Group Northampton page: about eight weeks and more than 250 manual operations per shoe
craft_evidence.reasoning: Church's owns its Northampton factory (Church & Co ltd, manufacturing, in Prada's group structure; St James Road since 1957) and documents Goodyear welting and the 250-operation process, so the English-made core is maker-and-brand-the-same. But sneakers, sandals, slippers and some boots are stated Made in Italy with no maker named, so owned making does not cover the whole range: a 4, not a 5. No mills or tanneries are named.

ownership.owner: Prada S.p.A. (Prada Group), acquired 1999; subsidiaries Church & Co ltd (manufacturing/services) and Church & Co (Footwear) ltd (trademarks), Northampton

opview: “Church's men's loafers are a true archetype of English style, originally evolving from a house slipper created for King George VI.” — Church's (the house, writing as itself), Church's US site, men's loafers category copy
